paragraphs: Here's what I see in this passage, friend. The Danites had a tribe to move and no land yet, and they went looking for a place to live. The story opens with "In those days there was no king in Israel" (Judges 18:1), and everybody in it is doing what makes sense to them. Nobody stops to ask what God wants, and that's where the trouble starts.

Look at how much of this sounds spiritual. The priest tells the spies, "Go in peace. The LORD is watching over your journey" (Judges 18:6), and then the same man takes the idols along for the ride (Judges 18:20). The Danites set up Micah's graven image for themselves (Judges 18:31), and it stayed there the whole time the house of God was in Shiloh. Friend, God's house was RIGHT THERE. They had the real thing down the road and picked the homemade one instead.

So here's my big idea for you. Using God's name is not the same as following God. A nice religious sentence can sit on top of a choice that never asked Him anything. Today, before you make the big move, ask what the Lord says about it first, and take the answer from His Word, not from whoever happens to say what you were hoping to hear. And this story isn't over, friend, because there's more in the Book of Judges, so keep baking.
